call_config_controlbox(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateConfigSDK, *, robot_model: str, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_CallConfigControlBoxTD#

Requests the cobot’s full control-box configuration snapshot.

Returns the aggregate configuration written by this class’s various save_*/set_* control-box-related calls: side/ext digital I/O special function and filter settings, the 8 area configs, and the 8 user frame configs.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_CallConfigControlBoxT containing the control box configuration snapshot.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

pub_realtime_index(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateConfigSDK, *, robot_model: str, target_index: int, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → None#

Publishes the realtime index of the robot.

Publishes a message to change the realtime index of the specified robot model to target_index. Unlike set_realtime_index(), this uses the publish/subscribe channel and does not wait for a response from the receiver.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • target_index – Realtime index value to apply.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the message has been published.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the result of the publish request.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the message cannot be published.

save_collision_parameter(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateConfigSDK, *, robot_model: str, onoff: int, react: int, threshold: float, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to save its out collision detection parameters.

Persist-and-apply counterpart to set_out_collision_para: writes to persistent storage and then applies it immediately, whereas set_out_collision_para only applies it for the current session (lost on restart). Same out_coll_onoff/out_coll_react/out_coll_limit fields reported by call_config_robotarm.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • onoff – Enables/disables collision detection: 0 Off, 1 On.

  • react – Reaction behavior when a collision is detected: 0 Pause Movement, 1 Evasion Stop.

  • threshold – Collision detection sensitivity threshold (clamped to 0–1 by the robot); lower values trigger a stop at weaker impacts.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the save request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

Requests the cobot to capture its current pose into a named global pin slot.

Saves the robot’s current joint values and Cartesian pose (at the moment this is called) into the given pin slot under pin_name. call_move_home's home_type = 3 + pin_num moves the robot to this pin’s joint pose (Move-J) or Cartesian pose (Move-L).

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • pin_num – Global pin slot number, 0-15.

  • pin_name – Display name for the pin.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the save request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

save_robot_code(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateConfigSDK, *, robot_model: str, code: int, option: int, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to save its robot model/hardware code.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • code – Robot model/hardware code to save. Takes effect only after the robot control program is restarted.

  • option – Accepted but currently unused by the robot firmware.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the save request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

Warning

code identifies which hardware/kinematics parameter set the robot loads. It is written to persistent storage but does NOT take effect until the next reboot (the firmware source marks this “NO ADJUST” — no live re-apply happens). If code doesn’t match a known robot model, the parameter set loaded on next boot can be invalid, and the robot control program can fail to initialize / crash immediately on restart. Do not call this with a value that isn’t a known, correct model code for this physical robot.

save_selfcoll_parameter(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateConfigSDK, *, robot_model: str, mode: int, dist_internal: float, dist_external: float, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to save its self-collision detection parameters.

Persist-and-apply counterpart to set_self_collision_para: writes to persistent storage and then applies it immediately, whereas set_self_collision_para only applies it for the current session (lost on restart). Same self_coll_mode/self_coll_distance_inter/self_coll_distance_exter fields reported by call_config_robotarm.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • mode – Self-collision detection mode: 0 stop just before self- collision, 1 control speed during self-collision.

  • dist_internal – Internal self-collision distance (mm) threshold, floored at 0 by the robot.

  • dist_external – External self-collision distance (mm) threshold, floored at 0 by the robot.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the save request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

Requests the cobot to save a tool’s parameters into its tool list.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • tool_no – Tool slot number to save into, 0-7.

  • tool_name – Display name for the tool.

  • tcp_x – TCP offset from the flange along X, in mm.

  • tcp_y – TCP offset from the flange along Y, in mm.

  • tcp_z – TCP offset from the flange along Z, in mm.

get_absolute_value(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateGetDataSDK, *, robot_model: str, reference_value: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, move_type: int, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_Get_Absolute_ValueTD#

Computes the absolute coordinate a reference target resolves to.

Used internally for absolute (non-relative) target resolution, e.g. by set_pin_point_or_joint when no reference_target offset is given. reference_value's tar_frame does not need to match move_type: the robot always converts it (forward/inverse kinematics as needed) to the frame matching move_type. This conversion can itself fail (e.g. an unreachable target), which surfaces as a nonzero calculated_result.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • reference_value – Reference target and frame information. tar_values must resolve to exactly 7 elements — this SDK truncates it to at most 7, so supplying fewer than 7 will not be padded and the request will be rejected.

  • move_type – 0 for the move-J / pin-joint family (joint-space), 1 for the move-L / pin-point family (Cartesian-space).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_Get_Absolute_ValueT with calculated_result (0 on success) and calculated_value (the computed absolute target). If tar_values doesn’t resolve to exactly 7 elements, the robot rejects the request before any calculation runs: calculated_result is nonzero and calculated_value is left unset.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query itself fails (e.g. no reply).

Note

This function does not throw on calculation failure — calculated_result nonzero must be checked by the caller.

get_relative_value(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateGetDataSDK, *, robot_model: str, relative_value: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, reference_value: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, move_type: int, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_Get_Relative_ValueTD#

Computes the coordinate a relative move would resolve to.

Given reference_value as the starting point, computes the absolute target that moving by relative_value from it resolves to. Used internally by the move-family functions’ relative-move calculation (e.g. call_move_j / call_move_l).

relative_value and reference_value do not need the same tar_frame: if one is Joint Space (tar_frame -1) and the other isn’t, the robot converts one to match the other (forward/inverse kinematics) before combining them, then converts the combined result again if needed to match move_type. This conversion can itself fail (e.g. an unreachable target), which surfaces as a nonzero calculated_result.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • relative_value – Relative offset target and frame information. tar_values must have exactly 7 elements — this SDK passes it through unmodified, so callers must pad to 7 themselves (e.g. with 0 for a 6-axis model’s unused ArmAngle slot).

  • reference_value – Reference target and frame information. tar_values must resolve to exactly 7 elements after this SDK truncates it to at most 7 — supplying fewer than 7 will not be padded and will fail the same way as an oversized/undersized relative_value.

  • move_type – 0 for the move-J family (joint-space), 1 for the move-L family (Cartesian-space).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_Get_Relative_ValueT with calculated_result (0 on success) and calculated_value (the computed absolute target). If either tar_values doesn’t resolve to exactly 7 elements, the robot rejects the request before any calculation runs: calculated_result is nonzero and calculated_value is left unset.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query itself fails (e.g. no reply).

Note

This function does not throw on calculation failure — calculated_result nonzero must be checked by the caller (as the move-family functions do).

get_variable(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateGetDataSDK, *, robot_model: str, name: str) → float | list[float] | str | None#

Looks up a named runtime variable/system value on the robot.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • name – Variable name to query.

Returns:

The variable’s value as a float, a list of floats, or a string, depending on its reported type; std::nullopt if the response is invalid or the response’s type doesn’t match any of those. This matches the Python original.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query itself fails (e.g. no reply).

get_variables(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateGetDataSDK, *, robot_model: str, names: list[str]) → dict[str, float | list[float] | str | None]#

Reads several core variables in a single query.

Same as calling get_variable once per name, but sends one get_core_data_multi query instead of one query per name, so the values also come from the same moment in time.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • names – Variable names to read.

Returns:

A map from variable name to its value (a float, a list of floats, or a string, depending on its reported type). A name the robot reports as invalid maps to std::nullopt, and a name missing from the response is absent from the map.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query itself fails. A robot whose core does not serve get_core_data_multi answers nothing, which surfaces as rb_zenoh::ZenohNoReply; fall back to get_variable per name in that case.

  • desired_out – Desired output value. A negative value is a no-op (the robot returns success without changing any output).

call_ext_dout_bitcombination(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateIOSDK, *, robot_model: str, port_start: int, port_end: int, desired_value: int, direction_option: int, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to set a range of extension board digital outputs at once.

Ports that have a special function assigned (see save_ext_dout_function) are rejected — this call only works on plain digital output ports.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • port_start – First port number in the range (inclusive).

  • port_end – Last port number in the range (inclusive), must be >= port_start.

  • desired_value – Bit pattern of output values to apply across the port range. Let N = port_end - port_start + 1 (number of ports in the range); valid range is 0 to (2^N - 1), one bit per port.

  • direction_option – Direction to map bits to ports: 0 applies bit 0 to port_start (normal), 1 applies bit 0 to port_end (inverse).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails, no payload is returned, or the response’s return_value is nonzero.

call_ext_dout_pulse(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateIOSDK, *, robot_model: str, port_num: int, block_mode: int, direction: int, time_1: float, time_2: float, time_3: float, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to pulse an extension board digital output on a timing schedule.

Ports that have a special function assigned (see save_ext_dout_function) are rejected — this call only works on plain digital output ports.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • port_num – Extension board digital output port number (0-15).

  • block_mode – 0 blocks until the pulse sequence finishes (up to a 10-second internal wait) before returning; 1 returns immediately without waiting. Any value other than 1 is treated as 0.

  • direction – Pulse waveform pattern across the 3 time segments: 0 for off/on/off, 1 for on/off/on. Any value other than 1 is treated as 0.

  • time_1 – First timing parameter, in seconds (valid range 0-3).

  • time_2 – Second timing parameter, in seconds (valid range 0-3).

  • time_3 – Third timing parameter, in seconds (valid range 0-3). Values below 0.003 are silently raised to 0.003 by the robot (unlike time_1 / time_2, which are used as given).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails, no payload is returned, or the response’s return_value is nonzero.

Note

The query timeout may increase based on the sum of the requested pulse times (time_1, time_2, and time_3).

call_side_dout_bitcombination(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateIOSDK, *, robot_model: str, port_start: int, port_end: int, desired_value: int, direction_option: int, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to set a range of side board digital outputs at once.

Ports that have a special function assigned (see save_side_dout_function) are rejected — this call only works on plain digital output ports.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • port_start – First port number in the range (inclusive).

  • port_end – Last port number in the range (inclusive), must be >= port_start.

  • desired_value – Bit pattern of output values to apply across the port range. Let N = port_end - port_start + 1 (number of ports in the range); valid range is 0 to (2^N - 1), one bit per port.

  • direction_option – Direction to map bits to ports: 0 applies bit 0 to port_start (normal), 1 applies bit 0 to port_end (inverse).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails, no payload is returned, or the response’s return_value is nonzero.

call_side_dout_pulse(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateIOSDK, *, robot_model: str, port_num: int, block_mode: int, direction: int, time_1: float, time_2: float, time_3: float, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to pulse a side board digital output on a timing schedule.

Ports that have a special function assigned (see save_side_dout_function) are rejected — this call only works on plain digital output ports.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • port_num – Side board digital output port number (0-15).

  • block_mode – 0 blocks until the pulse sequence finishes (up to a 10-second internal wait) before returning; 1 returns immediately without waiting. Any value other than 1 is treated as 0.

  • direction – Pulse waveform pattern across the 3 time segments: 0 for off/on/off, 1 for on/off/on. Any value other than 1 is treated as 0.

  • time_1 – First timing parameter, in seconds (valid range 0-3).

  • time_2 – Second timing parameter, in seconds (valid range 0-3).

  • time_3 – Third timing parameter, in seconds (valid range 0-3). Values below 0.003 are silently raised to 0.003 by the robot (unlike time_1 / time_2, which are used as given).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails, no payload is returned, or the response’s return_value is nonzero.

Note

The query timeout may increase based on the sum of the requested pulse times (time_1, time_2, and time_3).

call_joint_sensor_reset(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateMaintenanceSDK, *, robot_model: str, board_no: int, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to run a joint board’s current-sensor calibration procedure.

This is a multi-stage physical calibration, not an instant reset: cycles the brake and runs DQ-axis alignment (3 tries), DQ save (2 tries), and current nulling (2 tries), with real delays between steps. Takes on the order of several seconds per joint. Powers the robot on first if it isn’t already powered.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • board_no – Joint board number to calibrate. A negative value applies to every joint board (multiplying the total time).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails, board_no is out of range, or the result cannot be retrieved.

Requests the cobot to log/broadcast a joint board’s big-error/input- error pulse thresholds.

Counterpart to set_joint_big_input, but this does not return the threshold values through the SDK call — the robot only reports success/failure here. The actual values are logged and broadcast as a general message on the robot side (visible on the teach-pendant/UI, not returned to this caller). Also powers the robot on if it isn’t already.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • board_no – Joint board number to query. A negative value queries every joint board.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing only success/failure — no threshold payload.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails, board_no is out of range, or the result cannot be retrieved.

Same fields as call_admittance_force_on except sensor/contact- force settings, which cannot be changed while active.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • frame – Target frame: 0 Global, 1 Local, 2 User, 3 Target.

  • enable_x – Enable X axis (0/1, default 0/unchecked).

  • enable_y – Enable Y axis (0/1, default 0/unchecked).

  • enable_z – Enable Z axis (0/1, default 0/unchecked).

  • enable_rx – Enable Rx axis (0/1, default 0/unchecked).

  • enable_ry – Enable Ry axis (0/1, default 0/unchecked).

  • enable_rz – Enable Rz axis (0/1, default 0/unchecked).

  • target_x – Target force/torque along X (default 0).

  • target_y – Target force/torque along Y (default 0).

  • target_z – Target force/torque along Z (default 0).

  • target_rx – Target force/torque around Rx (default 0).

  • target_ry – Target force/torque around Ry (default 0).

  • target_rz – Target force/torque around Rz (default 0).

  • pgain_x – X-axis P gain (default 1).

  • pgain_y – Y-axis P gain (default 1).

  • pgain_z – Z-axis P gain (default 1).

  • pgain_rx – Rx-axis P gain (default 1).

  • pgain_ry – Ry-axis P gain (default 1).

  • pgain_rz – Rz-axis P gain (default 1).

  • igain_x – X-axis I gain (default 0).

  • igain_y – Y-axis I gain (default 0).

  • igain_z – Z-axis I gain (default 0).

  • igain_rx – Rx-axis I gain (default 0).

  • igain_ry – Ry-axis I gain (default 0).

  • igain_rz – Rz-axis I gain (default 0).

  • spdlim_x – X-axis speed limit (default 0).

  • spdlim_y – Y-axis speed limit (default 0).

  • spdlim_z – Z-axis speed limit (default 0).

  • spdlim_rx – Rx-axis speed limit (default 0).

  • spdlim_ry – Ry-axis speed limit (default 0).

  • spdlim_rz – Rz-axis speed limit (default 0).

  • max_dev_pos – Position max deviation, in mm.

  • max_dev_rot – Rotation max deviation, in degrees.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

call_move_j(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateMoveSDK, *, robot_model: str, target: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, reference_value: list[float] | None = None, speed: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_SpeedTD | None = None, ext_axis: list[float] | None = None, properties: list[rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Move_Property_EntryTD] | None = None, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to start a J-type (joint-space) movement.

Supports J-type (joint-space) movement of the cobot: the target is given as a per-joint angle set, and each joint moves independently toward its target angle, so the resulting end-effector path is not constrained to a straight line (as opposed to L-type movement). If reference joint values are provided, the target is calculated as a relative movement from the reference position.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • target – Target position and frame information. When reference_value is provided, tar_values must have exactly 7 elements (the underlying relative-value calculation rejects any other length).

  • reference_value – Optional reference joint values used for relative movement calculation. Must have exactly 7 elements when provided — e.g. [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0].

  • speed – Optional movement speed parameters.

  • ext_axis – Optional external axis values.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the movement result is reported to the flow manager and completion is handled asynchronously.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the movement request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If relative movement calculation fails, or if the movement result cannot be retrieved.

Note

If speed is not provided, the default values are: spd_mode = 1, spd_vel_para = 60, spd_acc_para = 120.

Note

If flow_manager_args is provided, this function returns immediately after submitting the request; a background monitor waits for the actual motion-completion signal from the robot before invoking the flow manager’s completion callback. If args[“variable”] is set, the final joint_q_ref is stored in that variable before completion.

call_move_jb_add(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateMoveSDK, *, robot_model: str, target: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, reference_value: list[float] | None = None, speed: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_SpeedTD | None = None, blend_type: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TypeTD, ext_axis: list[float] | None = None, properties: list[rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Move_Property_EntryTD] | None = None, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to add a segment to the queued joint-blend movement sequence.

Appends one joint-space segment to the internal blend list built up across successive calls; the queued segments run together once call_move_jb_run is invoked. If reference joint values are provided, the segment’s target is calculated as a relative movement from the reference position.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • target – Target position and frame information. When reference_value is provided, tar_values must have exactly 7 elements (the underlying relative-value calculation rejects any other length).

  • reference_value – Optional reference joint values used for relative movement calculation. Must have exactly 7 elements when provided — e.g. [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0].

  • speed – Optional movement speed parameters.

  • blend_type – Blend transition parameters. pnt_type is 0 (Percentage) or 1 (Distance); pnt_para is a percentage when pnt_type is 0, or millimeters when pnt_type is 1.

  • ext_axis – Optional external axis values.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, this segment is recorded for the blend sequence and completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous), unlike run commands whose completion is tracked asynchronously.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the add request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If relative movement calculation fails, or if the add request result cannot be retrieved.

Note

If speed is not provided, the default values are: spd_mode = 1, spd_vel_para = 60, spd_acc_para = 120.

call_move_l(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateMoveSDK, *, robot_model: str, target: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, reference_value: list[float] | None = None, speed: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_SpeedTD | None = None, ext_axis: list[float] | None = None, properties: list[rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Move_Property_EntryTD] | None = None, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to start an L-type (linear/Cartesian-space) movement.

Supports L-type (linear/Cartesian-space) movement of the cobot: the target is given as a Cartesian pose, and the end-effector moves in a straight line to that pose (as opposed to J-type movement). If reference_value is provided, the target is calculated as a relative movement from the reference position.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • target – Target position and frame information. tar_values is [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, aa] for 7-axis models, or [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz] for 6-axis models (aa = ArmAngle). When reference_value is provided, tar_values must have exactly 7 elements regardless of axis count (pad with 0 for a 6-axis model’s unused aa slot) — the underlying relative-value calculation rejects any other length.

  • reference_value – Optional reference target used for relative movement calculation, in the same [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz(, aa)] format as target. Must have exactly 7 elements when provided, regardless of axis count.

  • speed – Optional movement speed parameters.

  • ext_axis – Optional external axis values.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the movement result is reported to the flow manager and completion is handled asynchronously.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the movement request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If relative movement calculation fails, or if the movement result cannot be retrieved.

Note

If speed is not provided, the default values are: spd_mode = 1, spd_vel_para = 60, spd_acc_para = 120.

Note

If flow_manager_args is provided, this function returns immediately after submitting the request; a background monitor waits for the actual motion-completion signal from the robot before invoking the flow manager’s completion callback. If args[“variable”] is set, the final carte_x_ref is stored in that variable before completion.

call_move_wait(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateMoveSDK, *, robot_model: str, timeout_sec: float, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_Move_WaitTD#

Requests the cobot to block until the current motion finishes.

Waits, on the robot side, until whatever motion is currently running reaches completion (or no motion is running, in which case this returns immediately).

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • timeout_sec – Maximum time to wait, in seconds. A negative value (e.g. -1) waits indefinitely, with no timeout.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the response is received, provided its motion_result is 0; a nonzero motion_result raises before flow_manager_args.done() is reached.

call_online_j(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateMoveSDK, *, robot_model: str, target: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, speed: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_SpeedTD, timeout: float, filter: float, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to queue a joint-space online-tracking target.

Streaming/realtime joint control, intended to be called repeatedly (e.g. once per communication cycle) to keep feeding a moving target; if only one target is queued when the robot’s control loop next reads it, older undelivered targets are discarded and the latest one wins.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • target – Target joint position and frame information.

  • speed – Movement speed parameters — spd_vel_para/spd_acc_para act as the max velocity/acceleration for this segment and must be positive (not near zero).

  • timeout – Communication-loss timeout, in seconds (range 0-10): if no new target is queued within this time after the last one was consumed, the motion is considered finished. Rule of thumb: (1 / your call rate) + a small margin — e.g. 0.02 for 100Hz, 0.01 for 200Hz. Too small a value can trigger a false finish from ordinary communication jitter.

  • filter – Output smoothing filter value.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the movement result is reported to the flow manager immediately, and a background monitor invokes its completion callback once the actual motion finishes, instead of blocking here until then.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails, any input is non-finite or out of range, or the result cannot be retrieved.

  • timeout – Communication-loss timeout, in seconds (range 0-10): if no new target is queued within this time after the last one was consumed, the motion is considered finished. Rule of thumb: (1 / your call rate) + a small margin — e.g. 0.02 for 100Hz, 0.01 for 200Hz. Too small a value can trigger a false finish from ordinary communication jitter.

  • filter – Output smoothing filter value.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the movement result is reported to the flow manager immediately, and a background monitor invokes its completion callback once the actual motion finishes, instead of blocking here until then.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails, any input is non-finite or out of range, or the result cannot be retrieved.

Requests the cobot to queue a joint-space servo target segment.

Streaming/realtime joint control: each call queues one target segment to move smoothly toward from wherever the previous segment left off, rather than performing one discrete move. Intended to be called repeatedly (e.g. once per control tick) to stream a trajectory.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • target – Target joint position and frame information.

  • t1 – Time to move from the previous target to this one, in seconds (must be >= 0).

  • t2 – Additional hold/settle time after reaching the target, in seconds (valid range (0, 5]).

  • gain – Speed scaling gain applied to this segment (must be > 0).

  • filter – Output low-pass filter strength.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the movement result is reported to the flow manager immediately, and a background monitor invokes its completion callback once the actual motion finishes, instead of blocking here until then.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails, t1 / t2 / gain are out of their valid ranges, or the result cannot be retrieved.

call_servo_l(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateMoveSDK, *, robot_model: str, target: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, t1: float, t2: float, gain: float, filter: float, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Streaming/realtime Cartesian control: each call queues one target segment to move smoothly toward from wherever the previous segment left off, rather than performing one discrete move. Intended to be called repeatedly (e.g. once per control tick) to stream a trajectory.

Parameters:

  • gain – Speed scaling gain applied to this segment (must be > 0).

  • filter – Output low-pass filter strength.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the movement result is reported to the flow manager immediately, and a background monitor invokes its completion callback once the actual motion finishes, instead of blocking here until then.

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails, t1 / t2 / gain are out of their valid ranges, or the result cannot be retrieved.

call_servo_t(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateMoveSDK, *, robot_model: str, target: list[float] | None, time_out: float, option: int, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to start joint-space torque (compliance) control.

Unlike the position-based servo/online/timestamp motions above, this commands per-joint target torques directly rather than a target pose. The robot must be idle (no other motion in progress) when this is called, or the request is rejected.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • target – Target torque for each joint, in the same order as the robot’s joints. Must have exactly as many elements as the robot has joints, or the firmware rejects the request.

  • time_out – Maximum duration to hold this torque command, in seconds (valid range [0.0001, 10]).

  • option – Which compensation terms are combined with target: 0 Gravity + Friction feedforward + User target, 1 Gravity + User target, 2 Friction feedforward + User target, 3 User target only.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the movement result is reported to the flow manager immediately, and a background monitor invokes its completion callback once the actual motion finishes, instead of blocking here until then.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If target is not provided, the query fails, or the result cannot be retrieved.

call_timestamp_j(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateMoveSDK, *, robot_model: str, j_ang: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, j_vel: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, j_acc: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, polynomial: int, timestamp: float, timeout: float, filter: float, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to queue a keyframe-timed joint-space target.

Streaming/realtime joint control: each call queues one keyframe (angle, velocity, and acceleration) at a given timestamp along a continuous internal timeline, and the robot interpolates a polynomial trajectory between consecutive keyframes. This differs from call_servo_j, which specifies each segment as a relative duration (t1) from wherever the previous segment left off — here timestamp is a point on an absolute, ever-accumulating clock, so keyframes must be queued with strictly increasing timestamps.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • j_ang – Target joint angles for this keyframe.

  • j_vel – Target joint velocities for this keyframe. Ignored when polynomial is 2 (linear).

  • j_acc – Target joint accelerations for this keyframe. Only used when polynomial is 1 (5th order).

  • polynomial – Trajectory interpolation order between this keyframe and the previous one: 0 3rd order (uses j_ang and j_vel), 1 5th order (uses j_ang, j_vel, and j_acc), 2 1st order/linear (uses j_ang only).

  • timestamp – Absolute time, in seconds on the internal motion timeline, at which this keyframe should be reached.

  • timeout – Communication-loss timeout, in seconds: if no new keyframe is queued within this time after the last one was reached, the motion is considered finished.

  • filter – Output low-pass filter strength.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the movement result is reported to the flow manager immediately, and a background monitor invokes its completion callback once the actual motion finishes, instead of blocking here until then.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

call_wrapper_servo_l_on(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateMoveSDK, *, robot_model: str, target: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, time_gap: float, filter: float, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Requests the cobot to start (or queue a target for) wrapper-layer Cartesian servo tracking.

Streaming/realtime Cartesian control, similar in purpose to call_servo_l, but runs in the firmware’s separate “wrapper” motion layer (the same layer used by call_tcp_weaving_on, call_admittance_force_on, and call_base_conveyor_on) rather than the main move sequencer. Each call queues one target to move smoothly toward from wherever the previous target left off; intended to be called repeatedly (e.g. once per control tick) to stream a trajectory. Call call_wrapper_servo_l_off to stop tracking.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • target – Target position and frame information.

  • time_gap – Time to move from the previous target to this one, in seconds (valid range [0, 30]).

  • filter – Output low-pass filter strength.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails, time_gap is out of range, or the result cannot be retrieved.

class rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulatePointSDK(*args, **kwargs)#

Bases: RBBaseSDK

set_point(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulatePointSDK, *, robot_model: str, move_type: str, tar_frame_reference_point: list[float] | None = None, pnt_para: float | None = None, pnt_type: int | None = None, tar_frame: int, tar_unit: int, tar_values: list[float], spd_mode: int, spd_vel_para: float, spd_acc_para: float, ext_axis: list[float] | None = None, method: int | None = None, properties: list[rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Move_Property_EntryTD] | None = None, tcp_num: int = -1, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Dispatches a single-point move request to the matching move function in RBManipulateMoveSDK, keyed by move_type.

This is a thin routing layer: it builds the shared target and speed structs from the flat parameter list below and forwards the call to call_move_j, call_move_l, call_move_jb_add, call_move_lb_add, or call_move_xb_add, matching move_type against the string constants in MoveType (J, L, JB, LB, XB). See those functions’ docstrings for the full behavior of each move type (relative-move handling, default speed, flow-manager completion semantics, etc.).

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • move_type – Move type selector; must be one of the MoveType constants: “J” (joint-space), “L” (linear/Cartesian- space), “JB” (joint-blend add), “LB” (linear-blend add), or “XB” (XB-type blend add). Any other value is rejected.

  • tar_frame_reference_point – Optional reference position used for relative movement calculation, forwarded as the reference_value argument to the J / L / JB / LB routes. Not used for the XB route.

  • pnt_para – Blend parameter, interpreted according to pnt_type. Required (together with pnt_type) for the JB, LB, and XB routes; unused for J and L.

  • pnt_type – Blend type: 0 (Percentage) or 1 (Distance); pnt_para is a percentage when pnt_type is 0, or millimeters when pnt_type is 1. Required (together with pnt_para) for the JB, LB, and XB routes; unused for J and L.

  • tar_frame – Target coordinate frame: -1 Joint Space, 0 Global Frame, 1 Tool Frame, 2 User Frame, 3 Target Frame.

  • tar_unit – Target coordinate unit: 0 mm/degree, 1 meter/radian (a third value, 2 for inch/degree, appears in one SDK- internal comment but is not confirmed elsewhere).

  • tar_values – Target coordinate values, interpreted according to tar_frame and tar_unit.

  • spd_mode – Speed mode: 0 percentage-based, 1 absolute (physical) values.

  • spd_vel_para – Speed parameter: a percentage when spd_mode is 0, or mm/s (L-type) / degree/s (J-type) when spd_mode is 1.

  • spd_acc_para – Acceleration parameter: a percentage when spd_mode is 0, or mm/s^2 (L-type) / degree/s^2 (J-type) when spd_mode is 1.

  • ext_axis – Optional external axis values, forwarded to the J / L / JB / LB routes. Not used for the XB route.

  • method – Blend method option, required for the XB route only; unused for J, L, JB, and LB.

  • tcp_num – Tool slot number to activate before issuing the move, via set_toollist_num. -1 (default) leaves the currently active tool unchanged.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context, forwarded unchanged to the underlying move function; see that function’s docstring for its completion semantics.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the underlying move function’s request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If move_type is not one of the MoveType constants, or if pnt_para / pnt_type is missing for the JB, LB, or XB route.

Note

For the XB route, method is read via .value() without a null check; passing None for method while using “XB” raises a different, less descriptive error than the explicit checks used for pnt_para / pnt_type.

Requests the cobot to set its core data publication frequency.

Sets how often the robot publishes its periodic core-data state stream on the {robot_model}/state_core topic (IPC::State_Core — joint/ Cartesian refs, encoder values, etc.) that other parts of this SDK subscribe to (e.g. folder_finish_at).

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • frequency – Publication frequency, in Hz. The firmware clamps this to the range [0.1, 500.0] before applying it; the default rate before any call is 20 Hz.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

Requests the cobot to stop motion entirely.

Fully stops in-progress motion, as opposed to call_pause's temporary pause (which can be continued via call_resume).

Parameters:

robot_model – Name of the robot model.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the halt request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

Requests the cobot to pause motion.

Temporarily pauses in-progress motion; call call_resume afterward to continue from where it was paused.

Parameters:

robot_model – Name of the robot model.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the pause request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

call_program_after(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateProgramSDK, *, robot_model: str, option: int) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD | None#

Requests the cobot to run teardown after a program ends.

Called after a program finishes execution, pairing with call_program_before which runs beforehand. The firmware resumes any paused motion, stops all in-progress motion, restores the user- frame, area, out/self-collision, and TCP parameters that were in effect before the program ran, clears special DIN/DOUT masks, speed saturation, move-break, jacobian reflection mode, manual/landmark target shift, and fixed speed/time, and stops any running pattern.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • option – Currently ignored by the firmware (received but cast away unused); no option values are assigned or documented anywhere in the request schema.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result, or std::nullopt if the robot did not reply (or replied with an error) — that case is logged and swallowed so a silent robot does not block the program from finishing.

Note

Does not throw on a Zenoh no-reply or peer error response. Other runtime errors still propagate because they usually indicate local decode/SDK bugs rather than a silent robot.

call_program_before(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateProgramSDK, *, robot_model: str, option: int, monitoring_name: list[str] | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD | None#

Requests the cobot to run setup before a program starts.

Called before a program begins execution: the firmware stops all in- progress motion, clears special DIN/DOUT masks, speed saturation, move-break, jacobian reflection mode, manual/landmark target shift, fixed speed/time, and arc-sensing/pattern state, resetting the robot to a clean state for the new program. Also registers the given system variables to monitor while the program runs.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • option – Currently ignored by the firmware (received but cast away unused); no option values are assigned or documented anywhere in the request schema.

  • monitoring_name – Names of the system variables to monitor.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the request result, or std::nullopt if the robot did not reply (or replied with an error) — that case is logged and swallowed so a silent robot does not block the program from starting.

Note

Does not throw on a Zenoh no-reply or peer error response. Other runtime errors still propagate because they usually indicate local decode/SDK bugs rather than a silent robot.

Note

monitoring_name is optional; when omitted it is sent as an empty list

Note

The firmware requires the robot to be idle; if motion is still in progress it returns a warning result instead of performing the reset (this SDK call does not itself throw on that warning — only on a missing/failed response).

Resumes motion previously paused via call_pause, so the in- progress move/program can continue from where it left off.

Parameters:

robot_model – Name of the robot model.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the resume request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

folder_finish_at(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateProgramSDK, *, robot_model: str, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → None#

Starts background monitoring that breaks a Folder step’s children once its finish_at condition becomes true.

Used in PyFM: when a Folder step’s flow_manager_args carries a finish_at expression, this subscribes to the robot’s state_core topic and evaluates that expression against the PyFM context on every state update. As soon as it evaluates true, this calls call_smoothjog_stop with the evaluated stop_time, then breaks the folder (via the context’s break_folder) at the depth captured on entry, terminating the moves underneath that folder. Monitoring also stops on its own once execution has already exited the target folder depth. This is a no-op if flow_manager_args is not provided, or if its args do not have a finish_at value set.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • flow_manager_args – PyFM step context. Expected args: - finish_at: expression evaluated on every state update; monitoring only starts if this is set to a non- empty value. - stop_time: expression evaluated for the deceleration time passed to call_smoothjog_stop once finish_at becomes true (defaults to 0.0 if not set).

Note

flow_manager_args.done() is called immediately once monitoring starts, before finish_at ever becomes true — the PyFM step itself completes right away (so children can proceed) while the finish_at watch continues running in the background.

Note

Exceptions from the background monitor (e.g. from evaluating finish_at/stop_time) are caught and logged to stderr rather than propagated, since they run asynchronously in a subscription callback.

position_home(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateProgramSDK, *, robot_model: str, move_type: str, posture: object, project: str, spd_vel_ratio: float, spd_acc_ratio: float, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → None#

Moves the robot back to the begin position previously captured by set_begin.

Reads the MANIPULATE_BEGIN_* / MAIN_MANIPULATE_BEGIN_* PyFM local variables set by set_begin and issues a call_move_j or call_move_l back to that pose, scaled by the speed ratio also captured by set_begin. If none of those local variables were ever set (i.e. set_begin never ran successfully in this task), or if the specific pose requested by posture / move_type / project is missing, this is a no-op that only calls flow_manager_args.done(). A posture other than Posture::ZERO moves to the zero pose rather than to a captured one.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • move_type – Move type: MoveType::J for a joint-space move back to MANIPULATE_BEGIN_JOINTS, or MoveType::L for a Cartesian move back to MANIPULATE_BEGIN_CARTES.

  • posture – Posture::ZERO (Project Home Posture) reads the captured begin position and performs the move described above. Any other value (Posture::ONE = Joint Zero Posture) moves to a seven-value zero pose instead, without consulting the captured begin variables.

  • project – Project::MAIN reads the MAIN_MANIPULATE_BEGIN_* / MAIN_MANIPULATE_BEGIN_SPEED_RATIO variables (the outermost task’s begin position); Project::SUB reads the plain MANIPULATE_BEGIN_* / MANIPULATE_BEGIN_SPEED_RATIO variables (the current task’s own begin position, main or sub).

  • spd_vel_ratio – Velocity scale factor, multiplied by the speed ratio captured by set_begin (defaults to 1.0 if none was captured) to form the move’s spd_vel_para.

  • spd_acc_ratio – Acceleration scale factor, multiplied by the same captured speed ratio to form the move’s spd_acc_para.

  • flow_manager_args – PyFM step context. Required: passing nullptr raises std::runtime_error, matching the RuntimeError the legacy Python implementation raises for the same case.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If flow_manager_args is not provided, or if the underlying call_move_j / call_move_l fails.

set_begin(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateProgramSDK, *, robot_model: str, position: list[float] | None = None, speed_ratio: float | None = None, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD | None#

Captures the robot’s current pose into PyFM local variables as the task’s “begin” position.

Only operates within a PyFM step context: if flow_manager_args is not provided, this performs no action and immediately returns std::nullopt. Reads the robot’s current joint/Cartesian reference pose from the {robot_model}/state_core topic and stores it under MANIPULATE_BEGIN_JOINTS/MANIPULATE_BEGIN_CARTES in the PyFM local variables; if the current step is not inside a sub-task (its PyFM context has an empty sub_task_list), the same values are also stored under MAIN_MANIPULATE_BEGIN_JOINTS/MAIN_MANIPULATE_BEGIN_CARTES. If position / speed_ratio are given, they override MANIPULATE_BEGIN_JOINTS / MANIPULATE_BEGIN_SPEED_RATIO (and, for a main task, the corresponding MAIN_* variant) instead of the values read from the robot. Finally registers the resulting joint pose with the robot as its home joint info (set_home_joint_info: home_type 0 for a main task, 1 otherwise) so position_home can later move back to it.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • position – Optional joint-angle override for MANIPULATE_BEGIN_JOINTS (and MAIN_MANIPULATE_BEGIN_JOINTS for a main task); if omitted, the joint pose read from state_core is used.

  • speed_ratio – Optional override for MANIPULATE_BEGIN_SPEED_RATIO (and MAIN_MANIPULATE_BEGIN_SPEED_RATIO for a main task).

  • flow_manager_args – PyFM step context. Required in practice — despite the optional type, omitting it makes this function a no-op that returns std::nullopt.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT wrapping the set_home_joint_info result, or std::nullopt if flow_manager_args was not provided, or if reading state_core / setting the home joint info failed (in which case the begin-position local variables are instead reset to a seven-value zero pose).

Note

On failure (state_core read error or a failed set_home_joint_info result), MANIPULATE_BEGIN_JOINTS and MANIPULATE_BEGIN_CARTES are reset to seven zeros, the exception is caught and not re-thrown, and flow_manager_args.done() is still called so the PyFM step completes.

set_pin_point_or_joint(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateProgramSDK, *, robot_model: str, target: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_TargetTD, reference_target: list[float] | None = None, pin_type: str, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_Get_ValueTD | None#

Computes and stores a pin’s target value into the PyFM execution context.

Only operates within a PyFM step context: if flow_manager_args is not provided, this performs no calculation and immediately returns std::nullopt. When reference_target is given, the pin value is computed relative to it (via the SDK’s relative-value calculation); otherwise it is computed as an absolute value. If flow_manager_args carries a “variable_name” entry in its args, the resulting tar_values are stored under that name in the PyFM local variables.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • target – Target position/joint values and frame information used as the pin’s (relative) target.

  • reference_target – Optional reference values used for relative calculation; if omitted, an absolute value is computed instead.

  • pin_type – Pin type: “POINT” for a Cartesian-space pin, or “JOINT” for a joint-space pin.

  • flow_manager_args – PyFM step context. Required in practice — despite the optional type, omitting it makes this function a no-op that returns std::nullopt.

Returns:

IPC::Response_Get_ValueT containing the calculated value, or std::nullopt if flow_manager_args was not provided.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the relative or absolute value calculation fails.

rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Request_Set_SelfCollBlindTD | None = None, joint_origin_calibration: dict | None = None, wrist_singular_mode: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Request_Set_WristSingular_ModeTD | None = None, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → None#

Dispatches to the appropriate robot configuration setter based on option.

A single unified entry point for the many set_*/call_* configuration calls on RBManipulateConfigSDK: pass one of the SettingOptions::* constants as option, populate the single corresponding parameter below, and leave every other parameter unset. Throws if the parameter matching option is not provided, or if option matches none of the known SettingOptions values.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • option – One of the SettingOptions::* constants selecting which setter to invoke.

  • out_collision – Required when option is SettingOptions::OUT_COLLISION; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_out_collision_para.

  • self_collision – Required when option is SettingOptions::SELF_COLLISION; forwarded to RBM anipulateConfigSDK::set_self_collision_para.

  • user_frame_selection – Required when option is SettingOptions::USER_FRAME_SELECTION; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_us erframe_num. Both “user_frame_num” and the legacy program-args key “target_user_frame_num” are accepted; neither present throws rather than silently selecting user frame 0. That resolution runs in the dedicated type_caster at the pybind boundary (binding/glue/program_setting_caster.hpp); this function only sees the resolved UserFrameSelectionArg.

  • fixed_speed – Required when option is SettingOptions::FIXED_SPEED; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_fixed_speed.

  • target_shift – Required when option is SettingOptions::TARGET_SHIFT; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_shift.

  • speed_bar – Required when option is SettingOptions::SPEED_BAR; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::call_speedbar.

  • time_constraint – Required when option is SettingOptions::TIME_CONSTRAINT; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_timeconstraint.

  • ascii_function_call – Required when option is SettingOptions::ASCII_FUNCTION_CALL; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_asc ii_functioncall.

  • joint_impedance – Required when option is SettingOptions::JOINT_IMPEDANCE; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_joint_impedance.

  • free_drive – Required when option is SettingOptions::FREE_DRIVE; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_freedrive.

  • master_mode – Required when option is SettingOptions::MASTER_MODE; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_master_mode.

  • user_frame_6dof – Required when option is SettingOptions::USER_FRAME_6DOF; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_userframe_6dof.

  • user_frame_tcp – Required when option is SettingOptions::USER_FRAME_TCP; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_userframe_tcp.

  • user_frame_3points – Required when option is SettingOptions::USER_FRAME_3POINTS; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_userframe_3poi nts.

  • target_shift_landmark – Required when option is SettingOptions::TARGET_SHIFT_LANDMARK; the 6 reference/present points are rounded to 3 decimal places and padded to 7 values before being forwarded to RBManipulateCon figSDK::set_shift_landmark. Each point may be either a MoveInput_Target dict or, as legacy program args store them, a bare list of coordinates (taken as frame 0 / unit 0); that discrimination and the null check run in the dedicated type_caster at the pybind boundary (binding/glue/program_setting_caster.hpp), so this function only sees the resolved ShiftLandMarkArg.

  • program_flow_manage – Required when option is SettingOptions::PROGRAM_FLOW_MANAGE; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_pro gram_flow_manage.

  • din_function_mask – Required when option is SettingOptions::DIN_FUNCTION_MASK; forwarded to ``RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_din_function_mask. ``

  • dout_function_mask – Required when option is SettingOptions::DOUT_FUNCTION_MASK; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_dout_function_ mask.

  • jacobian_based_speed_control – Required when option is SettingO ptions::JACOBIAN_BASED_SPEED_CONTROL ; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigS DK::set_jacob_speed_mode.

  • self_vibration_mode – Required when option is SettingOptions::SELF_VIBRATION_MODE; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_sel f_vibration_mode.

  • vibration_motion_based – Required when option is SettingOptions::VIBRATION_MOTION_BASED. Passed from Python as a flat dict {“onoff”: 1/0, “frame”:, “x_mag”:, …}, matching the Request_Wrapper_VibrationMotion schema table and what the FE actually sends — not the wire request shape (Request_Wrapper_VibrationMotion_On / _Off, sent as two separate RPCs; “onoff” only selects which one to call). When onoff == 1, all 10 of frame/x_mag/y_mag/z_mag/x_freq/y_freq/ z_freq/x_phase/y_phase/z_phase must be present (each parsed via rb_glue::to_int / to_double, tolerating string-typed values from loosely-typed program args) or the request is rejected — the auto dict-to-struct caster would otherwise silently fill missing fields with 0. That validation runs in the dedicated type_caster at the pybind boundary (binding/glue/vibration_mo tion_caster.hpp); this function only sees the resolved VibrationMotionBasedArg. Forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::call _vibration_motion_on / call_vibration_motion_off.

  • external_axis_sync – Required when option is SettingOptions::EXTERNAL_AXIS_SYNC; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_external_axis_ sync.

  • tcp_speed_bound – Required when option is SettingOptions::TCP_SPEED_BOUND; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_tcp_speed_bound.

  • move_break – Required when option is SettingOptions::MOVE_BREAK_BLOCK; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_move_break.

  • joint_reference_filter – Required when option is SettingOptions::JOINT_REFERENCE_FILTER; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_ joint_reference_filter.

  • self_collision_blind – Required when option is SettingOptions::SELF_COLL_DETECT_BLIND; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_se lf_collision_blind.

  • joint_origin_calibration – Required when option is SettingOptio ns::JOINT_ORIGIN_CALIBRATION. The underlying dict’s “table_option” key (0: Clear, 1: Add, 2: Run (Calculate), 3: Reflect) selects which of RBManipulate MaintenanceSDK::call_origin_calib_clr, call_origin_calib_add, call_origin_calib_run, or call_origin_calib_reflect is invoked; missing “table_option” or a case’s own required fields throws. That resolution runs in the dedicated type_caster at the pybind boundary (bind ing/glue/program_setting_caster.hpp); this function only sees the resolved JointOriginCalibArg.

  • wrist_singular_mode – Required when option is SettingOptions::WRIST_SINGULARITY_MODE; forwarded to RBManipulateConfigSDK::set_wri st_singularity_mode.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context, forwarded as-is to whichever underlying setter is invoked.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the underlying setter’s result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the parameter matching option is not provided, if option matches no known SettingOptions value, or if the chosen setter’s own validation fails.

tool_out(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateProgramSDK, *, robot_model: str, tool_voltage: int, tool_dout_args: list[rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Request_Flange_Digital_OutTD], flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD | None#

Sets the tool (flange) power voltage and digital outputs.

Only operates within a PyFM step context: if flow_manager_args is not provided, this performs no action and immediately returns std::nullopt.

  • tool_voltage – Desired flange power voltage.

  • tool_dout_args – Digital output arguments to apply to the flange.

Requests the cobot’s safety configuration entries.

Pass a specific address in safety_addr to fetch a single entry, or -1 to fetch all safety configuration entries. Reads go through the same register table that save_safety_parameter writes to.

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • safety_addr – Safety config register address to query, or -1 to request all entries.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Requests the cobot to save a safety configuration parameter.

Writes target_value to the safety configuration register at target_addr — the write counterpart to call_config_safety's read. The firmware writes the value out over RS485 and, once acknowledged, persists it into the safety register table immediately (no separate commit step).

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • target_addr – Safety config register address to write. The firmware rejects addresses at or beyond the total number of safety registers.

  • target_value – Value to write to that address.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once the result is received.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the save request result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or the result cannot be retrieved.

Runs automatic TCP position calibration from a set of joint poses (Move > Calibration > TCP Position).

The robot is moved through the given joint poses and the TCP offset is computed from the resulting motion. Each entry in joints is rounded to 3 decimal places and padded/truncated to 7 values before being sent.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • joints – Joint poses to calibrate from. Each target’s tar_frame must be Joint (-1) — the values are joint angles, not Cartesian coordinates.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronously) once the response is received, provided its return_value is 0; a nonzero return_value raises before flow_manager_args.done() is reached.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the calibration result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or no payload is returned.

Every response field is a length-32 array indexed by PLC slot number.

  • min_p – Minimum position limit.

call_gripper_action(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateServiceSDK, *, robot_model: str, gripper_type: int, function_list: int, payload: list[float], flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Sends an Initialize command, plus any additional configured commands (e.g., Set-position, Action), to a configured gripper or end-of-arm tool.

A single generic entry point for all supported gripper models (Dynamixel, DH PG/CG/AG, Robotiq E-Pick/2F/Hand-E, Baumer LDS, OnRobot 2FG/RG/3FG/VG/VGC/MG/SoftGripper/VGP20/Sander, JRT JEG series, and others). function_list is model-specific: index 0 is always Initialize, and later indices are model-specific actions (e.g. Set Goal Position, Set Goal Pos/Spd/Force, Reset, Suction). The meaning of each payload slot depends on both gripper_type and function_list — each of the 23 supported gripper types has its own per-function payload layout (slot index, unit, and default value), too large to reproduce here in full; consult the gripper’s setup UI or vendor documentation for the exact slot mapping of the model in use.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • gripper_type – Gripper/tool model selector. 0 = Dynamixel Motor, 1 = DH PG/CG Series, 2 = DH AG Series, 3 = Robotiq E-Pick, 4 = Robotiq 2F Series, 5 = Robotiq Hand-E Series, 6 = Baumer LDS, 7 = OnRobot 2FG7, 8 = OnRobot 2FG14, 9 = OnRobot RG2, 10 = OnRobot RG6, 11 = OnRobot 3FG15, 12 = OnRobot 3FG25, 13 = OnRobot VG10, 14 = OnRobot VGC10, 15 = OnRobot MG10, 16 = OnRobot SoftGripper, 17 = OnRobot VGP20, 18 = OnRobot Sander, 19 = JRT JEGB, 20 = JRT JEGG, 21 = JRT JEGC, 22 = JRT JEGH.

  • function_list – Action to run for the selected gripper_type. 0 is Initialize for every model; the meaning of other indices is model-specific (see schema).

  • payload – Positional argument list for the selected gripper_type / function_list combination (e.g. connection port, device ID, target position/speed/force). Layout is model- and function-specific — see schema.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronously) once the response is received, provided its return_value is 0; a nonzero return_value raises before flow_manager_args.done() is reached.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the command result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or no payload is returned.

call_move_gcode(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateServiceSDK, *, robot_model: str, filename: str, gcodeframe: int, feed_spd_default: float, feed_spd_rapid: float, feed_spd_limit: float, feed_spd_rotation: float, default_plane: int, offset_x: float, offset_y: float, offset_z: float, will_const_sped: int, will_ignore_unknown: int, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Executes a G-code file as a robot motion program.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • filename – Name of the G-code file to run.

  • gcodeframe – Reference frame the G-code coordinates are interpreted in. 0 = Global, 1 = Local, 2 = User.

  • feed_spd_default – Default feed speed (mm/s).

  • feed_spd_rapid – Rapid (non-cutting) feed speed (mm/s).

  • feed_spd_limit – Maximum feed speed allowed (mm/s).

  • feed_spd_rotation – Feed rotation speed (deg/s).

  • default_plane – Default working plane. 0 = XY-Plane, 1 = ZX-Plane, 2 = YZ-Plane.

  • offset_x – X offset applied to all G-code coordinates (mm).

  • offset_y – Y offset applied to all G-code coordinates (mm).

  • offset_z – Z offset applied to all G-code coordinates (mm).

  • will_const_sped – Whether to run at constant speed. 0 = off, 1 = constant speed.

  • will_ignore_unknown – Whether to ignore unrecognized G-code commands instead of failing. 0 = off, 1 = ignore unknown code.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the run result is reported to the flow manager and completion is handled asynchronously.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the run-start result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or no payload is returned.

Note

If flow_manager_args is provided, this function returns immediately after submitting the request; a background monitor waits for the actual motion-completion signal from the robot before invoking the flow manager’s completion callback.

call_move_macro(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateServiceSDK, *, robot_model: str, type: int, corner_pnts: list[Sequence[float]], speed: rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.MoveInput_SpeedTD | None = None, rotation_mode: int, gap_num: int, margin_h_1: float, margin_h_2: float, margin_w_1: float, margin_w_2: float, margin_over: float, margin_over_para: float, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Runs a Motion Macro: a pre-built multi-segment move pattern (flat surface / round / triangle / 3D round) derived from a small set of corner points.

Rounds each point in corner_pnts to 3 decimal places, pads or truncates it to the 7-value tar_values format expected by the firmware, and forwards the request. The number of points required in corner_pnts depends on type: Flat Surface = 4, Round (R) = 6, Round (H) = 6, Triangle = 3, 3D Round = 9.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • type – Motion Macro type. 0 = Flat Surface, 1 = Round (R), 2 = Round (H), 3 = Triangle, 4 = 3D Round.

  • corner_pnts – Corner points defining the macro shape, each a [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, aa]-style value list (up to 7 elements; shorter lists are zero-padded). The number of points required depends on type (see above).

  • speed – Movement speed parameters used to run the macro.

  • rotation_mode – Orientation option. 0 = Intended, 1 = Constant.

  • gap_num – Gap number between macro segments.

  • margin_h_1 – Margin height 1 (mm).

  • margin_h_2 – Margin height 2 (mm).

  • margin_w_1 – Margin width 1 (mm).

  • margin_w_2 – Margin width 2 (mm).

  • margin_over – Margin over (mm).

  • margin_over_para – Margin over parameter, in the range [0, 1].

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the macro’s motion result is reported to the flow manager and completion is handled asynchronously.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the macro-start result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or no payload is returned.

Note

If flow_manager_args is provided, this function returns immediately after submitting the request; a background monitor waits for the actual motion-completion signal from the robot before invoking the flow manager’s completion callback.

Stops an active repeating Pattern by ID.

  • id – Pattern ID to stop, in the range [0, 29].

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronously) once the response is received, provided its return_value is 0; a nonzero return_value raises before flow_manager_args.done() is reached.

call_pattern_on(self: rb_sdk.rb_sdk_cpp.RBManipulateServiceSDK, *, robot_model: str, id: int, type: int, corner_pnts: list[Sequence[float]] | None = None, random_pnts: list[Sequence[float]] | None = None, count_x: int, count_y: int, count_z: int, anchor_pnt: Sequence[float], incremental: int, flow_manager_args: rb_schemas.sdk.FlowManagerArgs | None = None) → rb_schemas.fbs_types.ipc.Response_FunctionsTD#

Starts a repeating Pattern move: a grid or randomized sweep of points around an anchor point.

Builds the target point list from corner_pnts (for Line / Plane / Cube patterns) or random_pnts (when type is 3, Random), rounding each point to 3 decimal places and padding/truncating it to the 7-value tar_values format. The number of points required in corner_pnts depends on type: Line (X) = 2, Plane (X-Y) = 4, Cube (X-Y-Z) = 8; Random patterns instead take random_pnts, whose point count is caller-defined. Call call_pattern_off to stop.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • id – Pattern ID to run, in the range [0, 29]. Running a new pattern on an ID already in use is expected to replace it.

  • type – Pattern type. 0 = Line (X), 1 = Plane (X-Y), 2 = Cube (X-Y-Z), 3 = Random.

  • corner_pnts – Corner points defining the pattern grid, each a [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, aa]-style value list (up to 7 elements; shorter lists are zero-padded). Used when type is not 3 (Random); ignored otherwise.

  • random_pnts – Explicit point list used only when type is 3 (Random), in the same per-point format as corner_pnts. Ignored for the other pattern types.

  • count_x – Number of points to generate along the X axis.

  • count_y – Number of points to generate along the Y axis.

  • count_z – Number of points to generate along the Z axis.

  • anchor_pnt – Reference point the pattern grid is built around, as a [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, aa]-style value list (up to 7 elements; shorter lists are zero-padded).

  • incremental – Whether the pattern advances incrementally between activations (nonzero) or restarts from the first point each time (0).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronously) once the response is received, provided its return_value is 0; a nonzero return_value raises before flow_manager_args.done() is reached.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the pattern-start result.

Raises:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or no payload is returned.
